waypoints.name: Eightmile Lake Trailhead
waypoints.directions: The trailhead is reached via Icicle Creek Road and Eightmile Road (Road 7601), ending at the Eightmile Lake Trailhead at about 3,300 feet.

waypoints.name: White River Trailhead
waypoints.note: End of FR 6400 past Coles Corner/WA-207; $5 day-use fee or NW Forest Pass, self-issue wilderness permit at the kiosk, vault toilet, no potable water.
waypoints.directions: From US-2 at Coles Corner take WA-207 about ten miles up past Lake Wenatchee, then White River Road / FS-6400 another ten miles to the road end. Pavement gives out partway along; the gravel that follows is rough but not rutted, and the trailhead has a large gravelled lot shared with the Indian Creek, Mount David and PCT approaches.

waypoints.name: Boulder Creek Trail #1562 junction
waypoints.note: White River Trail's first 4 miles are flat, brushy, and often overgrown; bear right (east) off White River Trail #1507 onto the unmaintained Boulder Creek Trail #1562.
waypoints.directions: Head south on White River Trail #1507 along the valley floor. Four miles of nearly flat walking with almost no gain, brushy in places and notoriously mosquito-heavy from early to mid summer. Bear right (east) at the junction onto Boulder Creek Trail #1562, which is unmaintained above this point.

waypoints.name: Boulder Creek ford
waypoints.note: Unbridged, knee-to-thigh-deep crossing at the top of Boulder Basin depending on snowmelt; swap to sandals, current is swift early season.
waypoints.directions: Boulder Creek Trail climbs steadily through forest for about four and a half miles into Boulder Creek Basin. The creek is unbridged and must be forded; early in the season it runs cold and knee- to thigh-deep and often braids into two or three separate channels, which is easier to read but wetter than a single crossing. Sandals are worth carrying for it.

waypoints.name: Boulder Basin camp
waypoints.note: Established backcountry camp used as the standard base for a Clark summit day; the unmaintained climbers' path to Boulder Pass/Walrus Glacier splits off climbers-left just past the campsites and can vanish into brush.
waypoints.directions: A short walk past the ford puts you in the open basin, where established camps are spread between roughly 4,900 and 5,300 ft — around 8.5 miles and 3,000 ft from the car. Water is reliable here and essentially absent above it, so this is where you fill for the summit day. Given the scale of the outing most parties base here rather than attempt it car-to-car.

waypoints.name: Boulder Pass
waypoints.note: Scenic saddle with airy views over both the White and Napeequa drainages; the non-glacier south-side scramble and the Walrus Glacier line to the summit diverge from here.
waypoints.directions: Leave the maintained trail at camp and climb open heather and talus north toward the pass, picking up the climbers' path that breaks off climbers-left just past the campsites. It is a direct fall-line push and takes most parties around an hour and a half. Slopes in the basin below the pass hold wet-slide avalanche debris into early summer.

waypoints.name: Walrus (Clark) Glacier rope-up / crevasse zone
waypoints.note: Rope up here east of Boulder Pass before stepping onto the ~0.3 sq mi Walrus Glacier; stay on the left (south) margin, several narrow crevasses and one large crevasse crossed on a snowbridge.
waypoints.directions: Drop over the far side of the pass on steep snow to a bench around 6,700 ft on Clark's eastern arm, then traverse east across the basin beneath Peak 7242, crossing its northeast ridge at about that same height. Turn back west from there, roughly half an hour, to the toe of the glacier — it is labelled Clark Glacier on some maps. Rope up here with crampons and axe: the non-glacier south-side line diverges back at the pass, so stepping onto the ice is the committing choice.

waypoints.name: Clark Mountain summit
waypoints.note: True summit of the Dakobed Range's high point, 8 mi southeast of Glacier Peak; final approach is a short scramble over summit rocks above the glacier or south-side scree.
waypoints.directions: Take the moderately steep chute on the glacier's left (south) margin, stepping over several narrow crevasses and crossing one larger one on a snow bridge whose condition changes through the season and through the day. Above the ice a short Class 3 scramble over the summit rocks, with a soft 45-50 degree snow traverse below the top, gains the true summit.
